texts.preamble: M/S.Alina Traders vs The Commissioner Of Customs on 16 August, 2024 Author: C.Saravanan Bench: C.Saravanan W.P.No.12339 of 2 In The High Court Of Judicature At Madras Dated : 16.08.2024 Coram The Honourable Mr.Justice C.Saravanan W.P.No.12339 of 2021 and W.M.P.No.13117 of 2021 M/s.Alina Traders, Rep by its Managing Partner Mr.IRFAN Shaikh, Keregodi Road, Shanthi Nagar, Tiptur 572 201. Karnataka State. ... Petitioner Vs. 1.The Commissioner of Customs, Group 1, Chennai Ii Commissionerate, Custom House, No.60, Rajaji Salai, Chennai 600 001. 2.The Joint Commissioner of Customs, Group 1, Custom House, No.60, Rajaji Salai, Chennai 600 001. 3.The Deputy Commissioner of Customs (Siib), Custom House, No.60, Rajaji Salai, Chennai 600 001. ... Respondents M/S.Alina Traders vs The Commissioner Of Customs on 16 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14188758/ 1 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 1/6 W.P.N Prayer:
texts.facts: When the case was taken up for hearing on 09.08.2024, there was no representation for the petitioner. Hence, the case was directed to be listed under the caption "for dismissal". 2. In this writ petition, the petitioner has prayed for the following relief:- to direct the respondents herein to Release the goods 31 Tons Viz., 1240 Bags of Coconut Oil Meal https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Solvent Extract (Partially Defatted) variety for cattle feed, imported vide Ware Housing Bill of Entry bearing No.1006030, dated 15.03.2021, totally valued at USD 30,225.00 assessing the same under CTH 23065020 as correctly classified by the petitioner. In this connection, it is stated that the 3rd respondent has detained the goods imported vide letter dated 15.03.2021 and subsequently the examination was done and representative samples were drawn vide Mahazar dated 20.03.2021 and 22.03.2021. Later, the petitioner vide letter dated 24.03.2021 has requested to permit the cargo to move FTWZ Port for the storage to avoid the container detention, O-yard storage and transport charges. Based on the said request, the letter regarding movement of the said containers to J Matadee FTWZ, to avoid container detention, O-yard storage and transport charges, was issued on 25.03.2021 vide F.No.S.Misc.90/2021-SIIB(CH-III). Hence, it is stated M/S.Alina Traders vs The Commissioner Of Customs on 16 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14188758/ 2 that the SIIB has never seized the goods under Section 110 of the Customs Act, 1962 and thus the provisional release of the same under Section 110A of the Customs Act, 1962 is redundant. 4. In Paragraph No.12 of the counter affidavit, it has been https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis further stated that the oil content for the imported items is 45% and therefore the imported items appeared to be substandard goods with malafide intention of putting in the market for human consumption. Thus, the release of such goods till the completion of the investigations should not be allowed for the safety of the consumers. 5. It is noticed that imports were made by the petitioner as early as March 2021. The Bill of Entry bearing No.1006030 was filed on 15.03.2021. More than two years have gone, since, the imported consignments were detained by the Department for further investigation.
